title: Day-zero playground probe notes — Mar 2027
content:
Context: quick exploratory run in the Day‑Zero playground cluster (staging-play-3). Goal: repro a handful of customer day‑zero failure modes end-to-end, capture short remediation steps, and distill into a 1‑pager for field engineers. This is a working scratchpad — highly iterative, lots of todo items and hypotheses.

Attendees: Aisha (owner), Connor (networking), Sofia (install scripts), Evan (field eng) — ad-hoc: Priya joined for kernel/NFS notes.

Summary of probes performed (2027-03-15 -> 2027-03-17):
- Bootstrapped staging-play-3 with onprem package v1.14.2 (installer + agent).
- Ran three day-zero flows: fresh onprem node (baremetal), VPC customer mimic (AWS VPC with TGW), and hybrid (onprem + S3 model store via proxied gateway).
- Focus failures:
  * NFS mounts intermittently timing out on model pull.
  * KV cache directory permission mismatch on agent restart.
  * TLS handshake failure when KMS integration enabled (customer KMS proxy).
  * High tail latency when MTU mismatch between node and customer switch (packets fragmented).

Detailed notes by probe:
1) NFS / model artifact pull (customer-codename: phoenix)
- Symptom: model download stalls during first 10–20s after agent starts. Retries eventually succeed.
- Repro: mount large model bucket snapshot to /mnt/models via NFS exported from small VM (simulates customer onprem NAS).
- Findings: NFS server defaults to rsize/wsize that interacts badly with our threaded downloader under heavy concurrency; kernel-level lock contention observed. Traces show repeated EIO timeouts; support-bundle captured (support-20270315-phoenix.tgz).
- Workaround: lower concurrent fetch threads to 4 (was 12), add mount option noatime and set rsize=32768,wsize=32768.
- Action items: Sofia to add conservative default for NFS mounts in onprem installer (PATCH: private-install-scripts#142). Connor to draft KB on NFS tuning for field. ETA: 2027-03-22.

2) KV cache dir permission race on agent restart (customer-codename: atlas)
- Symptom: agent fails to start after abrupt restart; logs show EACCES when creating /var/lib/redwood/kvcache.
- Root cause hypothesis: installer creates directory as root:root, agent runs under redwood user on first boot, but a late-stage sha256 file is written by root during package postinstall, flipping perms.
- Repro: fast restart loop (systemd restart=always) triggered the race reliably.
- Fix: small fix in systemd service file to run a pre-start hook that chowns the dir. Sofia will include in v1.14.3. Quick patch applied in staging; needs more testing.
- Owner: Sofia. Status: in_progress. ETA: 2027-03-19.

3) KMS/TLS handshake failures (customer-codename: mistral)
- Symptom: controller cannot register key with customer KMS proxy; TLS error: "remote error: tls: bad certificate". Happens when customer proxy performs mutual TLS with a cert signed by internal CA.
- Notes: our validators currently only accept CA bundles from system trust store or explicit --ca-bundle path. Many customers embed their internal CA in a sidecar proxy.
- Temporary mitigation: allow explicit CA bundle path in agent config and document how to mount it via configmap/hostPath. Also add diagnostic to surface the server cert chain in the support bundle.
- Open question: do we ship a field-friendly way to ingest customer CAs securely (KMS-wrapped blob + auto-rotate)? Product needs input. Tagging product/security.
- Linked ticket: JIRA:PD-4872 (tracking product ask).

4) MTU mismatch & tail latency (hybrid scenario)
- Symptom: occasional 500ms+ tail token latency on short prompts when packets are fragmented; CPU spikes on NIC.
- Repro: set node MTU=1500 while customer transit link uses 9000. Observe retransmits and higher CPU from IRQ storms.
- Root cause: TCP segmentation fallback combined with application-level small writes causes syscalls and NIC thrashing.
- Workarounds: recommend aligning MTU end-to-end (documented). Add a networking probe in day-zero checklist that tests path MTU and warns if mismatch > 500. Connor will prototype quick probe (simple ping with DF + payload ramp).
- ETA prototype: 2027-03-24.

Operational checklist additions (proposed for onramp runbook):
- Preflight: verify path MTU and record to support bundle.
- Storage: if NFS present, include recommended mount opts and default concurrent download cap.
- Security: place explicit CA bundle handling section + how to add customer CA in secure way.
- Agent: ensure pre-start chown for kvcache; graceful restart paths.
- Observability: attach sample curl to KMS endpoint + certificate chain dump in support bundle.

Open blockers and ownership (current):
- KMS product decision: product/security needs to decide recommended pattern for customer CA ingestion and whether we support KMS-wrapped CA blobs (owner: Priya / product). Blocker: product review meeting scheduled 2027-03-19.
- Installer rpm conflict: when testing with node image that already has an older agent, rpm scriptlets conflict on postinstall hooks. Owner: Release Eng (tag release-eng). Workaround: rpm --replacepkgs in staging; long-term: deb/rpm package lifecycle policy.
- Field doc on NFS: owner Connor. Need to format into 1‑pager for field by 2027-03-22.

Decisions made during probe session:
- Do not enable aggressive concurrent downloads by default (lower concurrency default).
- Add a day-zero networking probe to installer and surface MTU mismatch as a WARN.
- Add pre-start chown to systemd unit; patch applied to staging.

Quick TODOs & next steps (short list):
- Sofia: land v1.14.3 hotfix with pre-start chown, add NFS conservative defaults (PR + QA) — ETA 2027-03-19.
- Connor: write NFS tuning KB and MTU probe POC — ETA 2027-03-22 for KB, 2027-03-24 for probe POC.
- Aisha/Evan: consolidate support-bundle samples and craft 1-page "Day‑Zero checklist" for field (draft by 2027-03-23).
- Product/Security (Priya): recommendation on CA ingestion pattern and acceptance criteria for KMS proxies — decision expected 2027-03-19.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could we ship a small lightweight agent-mode that only runs checks & sends diagnostics (no model pull) for initial day-zero? Would simplify first contact.
- Consider adding an init container flow for model pulls (separate lifecycle) to avoid agent restart races.
- Field team requested a one-click support bundle collection via console + agent endpoint. Ticket to propose UX.

Support bundles referenced in this doc: support-20270315-phoenix.tgz, support-20270316-mistral.tgz, support-20270317-atlas.tgz (stored in s3://redwood-internal/support-dumps/day-zero/).

If you pick something up, add initials and date next to the action to avoid duplication. Will sync next Tuesday standup (2027-03-23) to check progress.

-- Aisha

(attachments/links: GH PR 142 is a staging patch; see linked_artifacts above for details)
